1) Contracts will do a commercial + legal pass and return suggested redlines within 3 business days.
2) We’ll provide a short party-sheet (name, billing address, signing authority, technical contacts) and an evidence list for SOC2/KMS by EOD Monday.
3) If there are any high-priority SLA or data residency items, flag them in-line and we’ll fast-track review.

Tom / Markus — attaching our intake checklist and a first-pass redline summary in-line below. I reviewed Aurora_MSA_Draft_v1.pdf and noted the following commercial/legal items to prioritize:

- Liability cap: Aurora requests $5M; standard Redwood cap is 2x ARR (we need revenue band to evaluate).
- Indemnity: counterparty language is broad; propose adding carveouts for downstream third-party models.
- Data residency / subprocessor: redact clause needs clarification for sandboxing/analytics.
- Payment terms: Aurora asked for net-45; standard is net-30 — Laura to confirm flexibility.

Attachments / links: I uploaded a redline PDF to the Drive folder and included an annotated clause map (Drive link).

Action items:
- Tom: please confirm the Aurora signatory (full legal name and title) and whether Procurement has billing entity separate from operating entity.
- Markus: advise if we should propose a revenue-based liability cap alternative this cycle.
- Laura: confirm net-45 comfort and provide billing contact details to share with procurement.

Thanks — I’ll aim to post a tracked-change redline back to the Drive by EOD Tuesday.

Kimberly Park
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference

Kimberly — thanks for the quick review and for the checklist. Responding to the action items below:

- Signatory: Aurora Systems, Inc.; signatory is Maria Lin (VP Legal) — maria.lin@aurorasystems.com.
- Billing: Procurement confirms a single billing entity (Aurora Systems, Inc.) and they can accommodate net-45 for the initial term but prefer net-30 thereafter.
- Export control: not applicable for our use case (consumer-facing recommender).

We reviewed the liability cap conversation internally; Maria is amenable to a structured cap tied to first-year fees rather than ARR. We can surface numbers if that helps move things along.

I saw your Drive redline — looks comprehensive. Let us know if you want a short call with Maria to discuss indemnity carveouts.

Tom

Aurora Systems
